note: Mock DexFi stack. Real DexFi bonds exist only on Base mainnet, so MockUSDC/MockBond/MockFarm stand in and mirror the verified ABIs including the whitelist gate. The adapter is self-whitelisted here; on mainnet that is DexFi's call and is the one integration ask (PRD 14 ask #5).

riskParameters.divergenceNote: These are the values the DEPLOYED bytecode enforces, not the values Config.sol declares. This deployment is dated 2026-08-03 and predates two later changes: the capped-beta parameters agreed with DexFi on 2026-08-07 (2500 / 5000 / 25k / 5k), and the move of all four out of `internal constant` and into `RiskParams` storage. The deployed contracts have no RiskParams and cannot be retuned - the parameters are compiled in - so the divergence closes at the next redeploy and not before. Recorded as data rather than prose because it was prose for nine days and nothing could check it.
riskParameters.sourceOfTruth: the chain, read from RiskParams once a deployment carries one

operatorsNote: Owner, yield recipient, keeper and NAV confirmer are four distinct addresses, and every protocol contract was verified on-chain as owned by the configured owner rather than by the deployer. Read them from the contracts if you want them. The testnet operator keys are throwaways funded from a faucet; a mainnet deployment does not reuse that pattern.

state.liquiditySourceFundedNote: 250,000 mUSDC. This matched Config.GLOBAL_BORROW_CAP when it was funded and stopped matching on 2026-08-07, when the capped-beta cap dropped to 25,000e6 - the note went on claiming equality for nine days, off by ten times, because nothing read it. The float is deliberately left as funded: it is a testnet float and over-funding it refuses nothing.
state.navBootstrapNote: Seeded at the keeper's own independently reconstructed figure ($21.63780721), not DexFi's displayed $24.80. Bootstrapping at theirs would have put the keeper's first post outside the deviation budget on day one. bootstrapNav is one-shot (reverts AlreadyBootstrapped), so this cannot be corrected without redeploying the oracle and repointing everything at it.
state.navBudgetNote: The deviation budget is prorated by time since the last accepted price, so it reads 0 bps immediately after a bootstrap and any post parks for the confirmer. It accrues at NAV_MAX_DEVIATION_BPS (1000) * elapsed / NAV_DEVIATION_WINDOW (24h), so ~9 minutes covers 6 bps and a daily run has the full budget. Not a fault.
